appearance.title: Appearance
appearance.hint: The language applies to the screen, the CLI and the MCP (it is saved in the config.json on your machine). The palette and the theme stay in this browser.

settings.title: Settings
settings.intro: Rastro works without AI. With AI, it fills the gaps in the graph and writes the rules; everything it proposes goes through the compiler before it is accepted.

repos.title: Repositories
repos.intro: The code folders Rastro can read. The registered folder also powers the "Open in VS Code" button, which goes straight to the file and line.
repos.empty: No repository registered yet. Use the form below.
repos.noGit: no .git: the trace is saved without the commit
repos.commandsHelp: Runs in the repository folder. Write a single command, without chaining it with && or using | or >. Leave empty to skip it.
repos.removeText: The repository "{name}" leaves this list and Rastro loses its build and test commands. The traces already made stay saved. The folder on disk is not touched.
repos.removed: Repository "{name}" removed. The traces stay saved.

agent.title: Agent mode (MCP)
agent.intro: A coding agent, such as Claude Code, uses Rastro through the MCP tools and plays the role of the AI, under its own signature. You don't need a key here.
agent.hint: The agent uses the same traces and repositories as this screen (see the Repositories section). Everything it proposes shows up as inferred and waits for you to confirm it in the flow.

ai.title: AI (provider mode)
ai.intro: Rastro itself calls the AI with your API key. The keys are stored encrypted in Rastro's local storage and never come back to the screen.
ai.offIntro: Turn on AI to choose the provider, the key and the uses. What was already configured stays saved. When on, it does the following:
ai.offFillHoles: fill the gaps in the graph, proposing the target of calls the compiler could not resolve;
ai.offRules: write the rules of each step in your language;
ai.offOutro: Everything it proposes goes through the compiler and is only accepted after you confirm it.
ai.keepKeyPlaceholder: Leave empty to keep the current one
ai.useFillHolesHint: Propose the target of calls the compiler could not resolve.
ai.useDescribeRulesHint: Describe in your language what each step does.
ai.useContextHint: Suggest people and external systems in the context diagram.
ai.budgetHelp: Input plus output tokens per day. The counter resets at midnight UTC. 0 = no limit.
ai.budgetInvalid: The daily budget must be a whole number from 0 up.

unresolvedReason.multipleEndpoints: More than one endpoint handles the call

unresolvedReasonHint.multipleImplementations: The interface has several implementations and no DI registration decides which one runs here.
unresolvedReasonHint.noImplementation: The interface has no implementation in this solution. It may come from a package or from another repository.
unresolvedReasonHint.dynamicDispatch: The compiler did not link the call to a method (dynamic, or code that did not compile).
unresolvedReasonHint.delegate: What runs depends on who assigned the delegate or subscribed to the event.
unresolvedReasonHint.messageDispatch: The message handler is chosen at runtime by the mediator or bus.
unresolvedReasonHint.reflection: The method is called through reflection, so the target only exists at runtime.
unresolvedReasonHint.depthLimit: The path continues, but it stopped at the chosen depth limit.
unresolvedReasonHint.routeNotResolved: The HTTP call route is built at runtime, so there is no way to know which endpoint it reaches.
unresolvedReasonHint.noMatchingEndpoint: The route was resolved, but none of the chosen repositories has an endpoint that handles it.
unresolvedReasonHint.multipleEndpoints: The route matches more than one endpoint. Choose which one receives the call.

liveDb.title: Live database
liveDb.subtitle: Read-only connection to the database of {repository}.
liveDb.noConnection: No saved connection. Without it, Rastro reads only the code.
liveDb.label: Connection string
liveDb.keepPlaceholder: Leave empty to keep the current one
liveDb.testHelpTyped: The test uses the connection already saved. Save the new string to test it.
liveDb.testHelp: The test uses the connection already saved, not what is typed.
liveDb.savedNotice: Connection saved. The schema was read again. Next step: test the connection.
liveDb.removeConfirm: Remove the connection? Rastro goes back to reading only the code.
liveDb.grantsLead: Use a read-only user, with the minimum permission:

pg.connect: CONNECT is enough for the catalog. USAGE and SELECT apply to the estimated plan, because PostgreSQL also checks the statement permission in EXPLAIN. If you prefer, grant SELECT only on the tables you want to analyze.
pg.readOnly: The last one also makes the user read-only in the database.
pg.reads: Rastro reads only the catalog and asks for EXPLAIN without ANALYZE, on a read-only connection, without running the query.

liveDb.neverData: Table data is never read. The connection string stays encrypted in the local Rastro storage and never comes back to the screen.

sql.viewDefinition: VIEW DEFINITION is enough for the catalog. SHOWPLAN and SELECT apply to the estimated plan, because SQL Server only shows the plan to whoever can run the statement. If you prefer, grant SELECT only on the tables you want to analyze.
sql.reads: Rastro reads only the catalog (tables, columns, keys and indexes) and asks for the estimated plan, without running the query.

liveDb.testTitleTyped: Save the new string to test it
liveDb.missingIndex: The database itself points to a missing index on {table}, estimated gain of {impact}%
liveDb.missingIndexColumns: The database itself points to a missing index on {table} ({columns}), estimated gain of {impact}%

note.sqlServer: SET SHOWPLAN_XML: the database says how it would do it, without running the query. Parameters (@p0) go in as text.
note.postgreSql: EXPLAIN without ANALYZE, on a read-only connection: the database says how it would do it, without running the query. With a parameter ($1, @name), the plan is the generic one, which does not depend on the value.
